title: Shajar al-Durr
summary: Shajar al-Durr was a former enslaved concubine who became Sultana of Egypt following the death of her husband, the Ayyubid Sultan al-Salih Ayyub, in 1250. During the Seventh Crusade, she concealed the sultan's death and helped organize the defense that defeated King Louis IX of France. Her eighty-day sovereign reign and subsequent marriage to the commander Izz al-Din Aybak founded the Mamluk Sultanate, which governed Egypt for nearly three centuries.

uncertainty.note: Reigned as Sultana in 1250; died in Cairo on 28 April 1257; birth date unknown.
